audit.whatIsWrong: The chart and the prose disagree in three places, and the full layer's `diff` field says HARD while its own difficulty rating says 4/10 and its final rating line says 'Favoured matchup'. Specifically: win[2] said Ambessa while whys[2] says 'Illaoi takes it'; win[3] said Skill while whys[3] says 'This is your weakest window and her strongest'; win[5] said Skill while whys[5] says 'She edges the first-item window' and spikes[3] calls first item 'your turning point'.
audit.why: The true shape is a lane Ambessa wins overall with one real Illaoi window at levels 3-5, when her tentacle count is up and Ambessa's cooldowns are longest. After that Ambessa's dashes, the suppression and Grievous Wounds beat a champion whose damage needs you to be a Vessel or a Harsh Lesson target.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Ambessa / Ambessa / Illaoi / Illaoi / Ambessa / Ambessa / Ambessa in both layers — 5-2, matching 55.89%. whys[5] and whys[6] rewritten so the level 3-5 window is hers and everything after is yours. `diff` corrected from HARD to FAV, which is an existing value in this file and the only one consistent with 4/10 and 'Favoured matchup'.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike is written as a coinflip in which 'her R wall plus a slam erases you'. Leap of Faith spawns one Tentacle per enemy champion hit — in a solo lane that is exactly one tentacle, not a wall. Ambessa's own spike was credited to 'R passive armor-pen and ability-damage healing', neither of which is in Riot's text.
audit.why: Overstating Leap of Faith by an order of magnitude turns a favoured level 6 into a stage the player will decline to fight. Illaoi's real spikes are Test of Spirit ranking from 16s to 12s and her tentacle count; Ambessa's are the 130s Public Execution and the rank-5 Q at 10s.
audit.corrected: Level 6 rewritten as Ambessa's, with the one-tentacle fact stated. First item re-anchored on Q at 10s and Grievous Wounds rather than on penetration.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two of Illaoi's five abilities are never named on the page, including the one she actually presses most, and the single most important rule in the matchup is absent. Harsh Lesson — a 4-second, 30-mana leap that causes nearby Tentacles to swing at the target — is not mentioned once. And the page treats standing in the tentacle field as the danger, when Riot's passive text says Tentacles swing at spirits, Vessels, and victims of Harsh Lesson. Test of Spirit's actual failure condition is also missing: you become a Vessel if the spirit is killed OR if you get too far from it.
audit.why: This changes what a player does. 'Fight outside her tentacle field' is only half-right — the tentacles cannot touch you until she lands Harsh Lesson on you or you are a Vessel, so the thing to dodge is the leap, not the ground. And once Test of Spirit lands, running away is the losing move: distance from your spirit is what converts you into a Vessel and starts spawning tentacles on you. The right answer is to stay on the spirit and kill it, or to be already out of range when it is cast. Tentacles also spawn on impassible terrain, so the open middle of the lane is materially safer than the wall.
audit.corrected: Harsh Lesson named with its 4s cooldown in early, mid, wants.foe[1] and the interactions line. The 'do not walk away from your spirit' rule added to early, wants.you[0] and dontsFull[1]. Tentacle-spawn-on-terrain added to wants.you[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: Trading is keyed entirely to Test of Spirit's cooldown, which is the wrong timer for short exchanges.
audit.why: Test of Spirit is 16/15/14/13/12s and is the ability that decides whether you get punished for the next ten seconds, so it belongs to the all-in question. The trade-by-trade timer is Harsh Lesson at a flat 4 seconds — it is her gap-close, her auto reset, and the trigger that makes nearby tentacles swing at you, and she can afford to throw it at almost any time.
audit.corrected: early and mid now separate the two: dodge or pre-empt Harsh Lesson for trades, count Test of Spirit's 16s for commits.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page attributes Illaoi's healing to 'her W and slams'. Harsh Lesson has no heal in Riot's text; the healing is on the passive — Tentacles heal Illaoi when they damage a champion.
audit.why: Anti-heal is correctly called non-negotiable, but the player should know that the heal is per-tentacle-hit on a champion, which is precisely why staying off Harsh Lesson and out of Vessel status starves it even without an item.
audit.corrected: Attribution corrected in late and in the itemization reasoning.

audit.whatIsWrong: Critical Don'ts said 'Get E'd near a vessel'.
audit.why: Proximity to a vessel is not the failure state — walking away from your own extracted spirit is. That is what converts you.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to 'Walk away from your spirit'.

audit.whatIsWrong: The spirit-echo mechanic is never explained, though it is the reason the level 3-5 window is hers.
audit.why: Riot: 'Spirits echo a percentage of the damage they take to the original target.' Every point of damage Illaoi puts into the spirit also lands on you, which is how she wins a trade she is not even standing in.

edits.before: Level 1 is genuinely yours — Illaoi has one ability and no tentacles, so casting an ability for a Medarda Maxim empowered auto wins the straight last-hit trades. But the second her tentacles start stacking, the lane flips: do NOT stand in her field throwing Cunning Sweep. The whole early game is about her Test of Spirit — if it lands I'm fighting both her and my own torn spirit, so dash sideways out of the cast or bait it on a minion. By level 3 her Q-slam poke plus tentacle slams out-sustain my still-long cooldowns, so eat a little poke and farm at the edge of her tentacles instead of committing.
edits.after: Level 1 is genuinely yours — Illaoi has one ability and no tentacles, so casting an ability for a Medarda Maxim empowered auto wins the straight last-hit trades. Her tentacles only swing at spirits, Vessels, and whoever she lands Harsh Lesson on, so the 4-second leap is what you dodge, not the ground itself. And they spawn on impassible terrain, so the open middle of the lane is the safe half. If Test of Spirit does land, stay on your spirit and kill it — walking away from it is what turns you into a Vessel. By level 3 her Tentacle Smash poke out-sustains my long cooldowns, so farm at range and wait for six.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are Illaoi's window, not mine — my cooldowns are longest here and her tentacle field is dense, so I refuse extended fights inside it and trade only when Test of Spirit is down. At 6 it's a real coinflip: Public Execution blinks me behind her, suppresses, and drags her OFF her tentacles for a kill — but if she ults first, the tentacle wall and her slams delete me before my dash chain resets. Only press R when she's already E'd a minion or stepped away from her field; never ult into a fresh tentacle carpet.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are Illaoi's window, not mine — my cooldowns are longest while her tentacle count peaks, so I trade only when Test of Spirit's 16 seconds are ticking. Six is mine: Public Execution blinks 1250 units, suppresses, and drags her off her tentacles. Leap of Faith answers with one tentacle per champion it hits, so in a solo lane that is exactly one — respect the damage, not the wall. Commit once she has spent Test of Spirit, and stay off Harsh Lesson's 4s leap.

edits.before: My Eclipse and Q max are where I finally pull ahead — Cunning Sweep into empowered auto into Sundering Slam chunks half her bar while my R passive armor-pen and ability-damage healing cut the tankiness she's been hiding behind, and the energy refund on each empowered auto means I go again. She never falls off the way other bruisers do, though: her tentacles still shred grouped fights, so I want to catch her isolated and use Public Execution to yank her out of her field. Anti-heal (Bramble/Sentinel) is non-negotiable or her W and slams just heal everything back.
edits.after: My Eclipse and Q max are where I finally pull ahead — Cunning Sweep into empowered auto into Sundering Slam chunks half her bar, the rank-5 Q comes back in 10 seconds, and Drakehound’s Step refunds energy on every empowered auto so I go again. She never falls off the way other bruisers do: tentacles spawn on impassible terrain, so any grouped fight along a wall is hers, and I want her isolated in the open with Public Execution ready to yank her out. Anti-heal is non-negotiable — Prophet of an Elder God heals her every time a tentacle damages a champion.

notes: Important: champ-data/_kits/_missing-interactions.json lists 'Illaoi can go untargetable through your commit (Leap of Faith (R)) — wait it out rather than spending everything into it' for this matchup. That entry is derived from a bad flag. Riot's text for Leap of Faith is 'smashes her idol into the ground, dealing physical damage to nearby enemies. A Tentacle spawns for each enemy champion hit' — there is no untargetability and no grounding in it, and the kit file's 'grounding' flag has almost certainly fired on the words 'into the ground', the same misfire I found on Ambessa's own W and R. I deliberately did NOT write that interaction into the page, and the derive-interactions step that produced it should be re-run once the flags are fixed. Also unverified and removed rather than restated: Ambessa's 'R passive armor-pen' and 'ability-damage healing' (absent from Riot's text for all five of her abilities), and Harsh Lesson healing Illaoi (the heal is on the passive, per tentacle hit on a champion).
